findings.reason: the plan should cite and reuse the existing coverage rather than re-add a duplicate test, and should spend the node's budget on the binary and candidate-search branches that genuinely lack coverage.
findings.text: §6 proposes to add "the predicate's offending branch directly: a non-exempt path whose reader returns the root name is returned as an offender, and an exempt one is not", but `test_worktree_path_offenders_skips_the_exemption_set` already does exactly this (non-exempt `docs/figures/x/a.json` returned, four exempt paths skipped)

findings.reason: the design either applies the rewrite at both producers or states in its own text that this dump is out of the committed-artifact scope (its `--run-dir` default is `os.environ.get(_RUN_DIR_ENV, Path.cwd())`, not a tracked path), so a later reader is not left to rediscover it.
findings.text: §6 names `benchmarks/production_solve_host_profile.py` as "its producer" of the committed cProfile dump and wires the new rewrite helper to it, but `profiler.dump_stats(profile_path)` at this second site writes `cached-entry.prof` under `--run-dir` and embeds the same absolute worktree frame paths on every run from a worktree

findings.reason: unnamed, `_staged_files` survives and the guard has three enumerations over three different file sets (working tree, index, staged-only), which is the duplicate-owner defect the item exists to catch; the section must name `scripts.py` and the test helper as the sites it merges into `filepath`.
findings.text: §6 gives `nova/database/filepath.py` "one candidate search" so "the hook and the test share one enumeration", but the hook reaches the guard through `nova.database.scripts relativize --check`, which enumerates with `_staged_files`/`_staged_text` (scripts.py:37-52), and the test enumerates with `_tracked_files` (tests/test_artifacts_carry_no_worktree_paths.py:20-26); the plan does not name these two as retired by the new owner

findings.reason: with the week's public_definitions budget at 0, §6 must state in its own text what it retires or merges (the candidate search can retire `_staged_files`/`_tracked_files`; the adapter retires nothing) or why the addition is unavoidable.
findings.text: the section adds two public definitions to `nova/database/filepath.py` (the cProfile dump adapter and the candidate search) and cites no retirement or merge for either, and no reason none is possible

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §6 adds the rule's binary adapter and the candidate enumeration to the existing deep owner `nova/database/filepath.py`, behind functions smaller than the behaviour they hide, rather than spreading the guard across new modules.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `nova/database/scripts.py::_staged_files`/`_staged_text` and `tests/test_artifacts_carry_no_worktree_paths.py::_tracked_files` are parallel enumerations the plan means to merge into the new `filepath` candidate search but does not name, so the owner may gain a third.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6 adds two public definitions (the cProfile adapter and the candidate search) and names no retirement, nor why nothing can be retired.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the owner module well but did not search for the existing predicate-branch test (`tests/test_filepath.py:259`) it proposes to re-add, nor for the second `dump_stats` producer (`benchmarks/program_scope_census.py:1091`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the proposed cProfile helper is not a bare forwarder: it loads the dump, rewrites each recorded frame path, and writes the container back, work the rule alone cannot do; no existing shared pstats writer exists for it to extend instead.
